cases.note: a comma swaps the two parts only when it is the only comma; any other comma is punctuation
only the first token is dropped, only when it is a title and something else remains; the title is looked for after the comma swap
apostrophes vanish, every other mark is a space, digits stay; a name can be all digits
an email is only trimmed of surrounding spaces and lower-cased; a new record must use an unused id
a group needs the same normalized name and the same normalized email; records with neither are never grouped
the groups follow the records as they are added, and a record that is alone is not a group
empty text scores 0 even against itself; equal texts score 1; a window of 0 only matches the same position
transpositions are half the number of matched characters out of order, not rounded down
the prefix counts up to 4 characters and at most the shorter text; the boost applies whatever the Jaro value
the matching window is max(0, longest // 2 - 1) on either side, and each character matches once
tokens are runs of non-space characters taken as a set, compared exactly; two empty texts score 0
the name key is the first 3 letters of the last token, the email key is the whole email; either can be missing
a pair is compared when the records share a key, once however many keys they share; pairs come sorted
equal non-empty emails make the score 1; empty emails are never equal; a name that is empty scores 0 without a shared email
a pair in different blocks is never compared, so it is not among the matches even when it would match
a name written last-name-first is the same name; any other word order is not repaired, and moves the record to another block
the pairs are taken from the highest score down, not in the order of the ids
a merge needs every pair across the two clusters to score 0.65, not 0.75, so a chain of near names can still join
the guard compares every record of one cluster with every record of the other, matches or not
records with the same email are matches whatever their names, and the guard still looks at every other record of the clusters
the canonical record has the most filled fields, then the longest normalized name, then the smallest id; aliases are the other names
singletons are clusters too; ids sort as text; an unknown id has no canonical record and no aliases
clusters follow the records as they are added
a pair in different blocks is never compared, so records that would match stay apart, while the guard splits a chain that was compared
thirty people written in two to four ways each: clusters, aliases and canonical records
no pair predicted gives precision 1 and no pair in the gold gives recall 1; F1 is 0 when both are 0
pairwise counts grow with the square of a cluster, B-cubed weighs each record once: one big mistake against many small ones
the order of clusters and of ids inside them does not matter; errors come sorted with false merges first
recall below precision, and the reverse: F1 is the harmonic mean, and B-cubed is averaged over records before it is combined
the clusters of the larger run graded against the people they were written from
